turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Mr. Hale. Thank you for seeing me. I have twenty minutes.

I'm here about Owen's essay. You gave him a zero before you called me.

Walk me through it. What exactly did you see, and when?

I'm not here to be soothed, Mr. Hale.

I asked you a question. What did you see, and on what date?

Which tool gave the 94%? What did it flag, and where? Do you have the report?

And has Owen's zero been entered in the gradebook already? I'd like to know that first.
But I'm not changing the grade.

Then we'll start somewhere else.

Has anyone said anything to Owen's class? Yes or no.

Has anything gone to the office? Anything written in his file?

Those are the first things I need answered.

On the grade, I'm not asking you to change it today. I'm asking what it rests on. A score of 94% from a checker isn't evidence. It's a number.

So. Do you have the report? Do you have his drafts, or earlier writing from him to compare against?
I'm still not changing it. Keep going if you like.

Fine. I'll say where I stand.

Owen says he wrote it. I'm not asking you to take my word. I'm not taking yours either.

I'll take documents. The report, with its date. The school's policy on this tool. The date you entered the zero.

Here's what I need today. Nothing said to his class. Nothing in his file beyond the grade itself.

Can you tell me that, right now?

And the date you entered the zero. What is it?
You can say it ten more ways. The answer is no.

No to what, exactly?

No to changing the grade? I heard that. I'm not asking again today.

Or no to the other things? Telling his class nothing. Keeping his file clean. Giving me the date and the report.

Those are different questions. I want to hear which one you're answering.

Four years ago, my daughter got a zero in this building. She won her appeal. It came too late for her scholarship.

I won't sit through that twice. So I'm asking you plainly.

Is anything going to be said to Owen's class?
